issues.legal_issue: The demands required to exercise a right of pre-emption under Mohammedan law must be made after the sale is completed by the sale deed being copied into the registration books.
material_facts: The sale deed relied on in the dispute was copied into the registration books after the demand alleged to have been made by the pre-emptor.
The courts below had not examined the demands in light of the rule governing when the sale was completed.
issues.conclusion: For purposes of the required demands, the sale is completed when the sale deed is copied into the Sub-Registrar’s books; the date entered there is the date of sale. The Court did not determine whether the demands in this case were valid under that rule.
issues.legal_principle: Under Mohammedan law, the first and second demands are conditions precedent to exercising the right of pre-emption, and the first must be made promptly after the sale becomes known. Applying Ram Saran Lall v. Mst. Domini Kuer, the sale is completed when the sale deed is copied into the Sub-Registrar’s books, not merely when it is executed or presented for registration. The Court noted that this rule can make prompt compliance difficult, but regarded legislative change as a matter for Parliament.

predicates.pre_emption_suit: The proceeding is a suit to exercise a claimed right of pre-emption.
predicates.demand_precedes_record_copy: The pre-emptor made the required demand before the sale deed was copied into the registration books.
predicates.demand_is_premature: The required demand was made before the sale was treated as completed.

issues.definition: In a pre-emption suit, a demand made before the sale deed is copied into the registration books is premature.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the validity or timing of pre-emption demands that depends on the evidence cannot be raised for the first time before the Supreme Court when it was not presented to the courts below.
material_facts: The challenge that the pre-emption demands were premature was not raised before the courts below or in the special leave petition.
The timing and sufficiency of the demands had not been examined by the courts below under the applicable rule.
Determining the issue required consideration of the evidence, including evidence about when the demands were made.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to entertain the challenge at that stage, and the appeal arising from the pre-emption suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A point that is a mixed question of law and fact, and whose determination depends on the evidence, should be raised before and decided by the courts below; it is not just or proper to reopen it for the first time at the Supreme Court stage. The Court noted that the point had not been raised even in the special leave petition.

rule.if: supreme_court_appeal_in_pre_emption_suit and new_demand_challenge and challenge_depends_on_evidence and not raised_below

predicates.supreme_court_appeal_in_pre_emption_suit: The proceeding is an appeal before the Supreme Court arising from a pre-emption suit.
predicates.new_demand_challenge: A party raises a challenge to the validity or timing of the pre-emption demands at this stage.
predicates.challenge_depends_on_evidence: Deciding the challenge requires assessing evidence about the demands or their timing.
predicates.raised_below: The party presented the challenge to a court below.
predicates.new_mixed_question_not_entertained: The Court declines to decide the evidence-dependent challenge raised for the first time at this stage.

issues.definition: When an appeal in a pre-emption suit presents a new demand challenge that depends on evidence and was not raised below, the Court does not entertain that challenge.

issues.legal_issue: A later agreement cannot support specific performance against a seller when an earlier agreement concerning the property remains operative and capable of enforcement, and a competing right of pre-emption exists.
material_facts: An earlier agreement to sell the property had been made to the party who later claimed pre-emption.
The condition that the premises be vacated by a tenant had not been satisfied, so the earlier agreement had not lapsed and could be enforced.
A later agreement was made with the claimant seeking specific performance.
The courts below found that the party to the earlier agreement had a right of pre-emption.
issues.conclusion: The claim for specific performance under the later agreement was properly dismissed, and the appeal from that dismissal failed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the findings that the earlier agreement remained in force because its preliminary condition had not been satisfied, that its beneficiary could enforce it, and that the later agreement did not entitle the claimant to specific performance in the presence of the earlier agreement and the beneficiary’s right of pre-emption. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and earlier_agreement_remains_enforceable and later_agreement_claimed and competing_pre_emption_right_exists

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.earlier_agreement_remains_enforceable: An earlier agreement concerning the property remains in force and can be enforced by its beneficiary.
predicates.later_agreement_claimed: The claimant relies on a later agreement concerning the same property.
predicates.competing_pre_emption_right_exists: Another party has a right of pre-emption concerning the property.
predicates.specific_performance_under_later_agreeme: Specific performance under the later agreement is refused.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks specific performance under a later agreement while an earlier agreement remains enforceable and a competing right of pre-emption exists, specific performance under the later agreement is denied.
